originalTitle: Six Nigerians accused of romance scams to be extradited to the US
title: Big News! Learning About Being Safe Online!
content:
Hello, Super Reporters from Africa!

Hi everyone! It's your friendly news reporter, here to share some important news from our wonderful continent. My name is [Reporter's Name, e.g., Kiki the Cheetah], and I love sharing stories that help us learn and grow. Today, we're going to talk about something very important: staying safe when you are online or talking to new people. Let's learn together!

What's the Big News Today?

We have some news from a country called South Africa. The police there, who are like super helpers for everyone, have found six grown-ups. These grown-ups are from another country, Nigeria. The police say these six people did some tricky things online. Now, they are going to travel to a very far-away country called the United States of America. There, they will talk to a judge. A judge is like a grown-up who helps make sure everyone follows the rules and stays fair. They are going to the United States because that's where some of the people they tricked live. So, it's like sending someone to the right place to answer questions about what they did. This is a special thing called 'extradition.' It means sending someone from one country to another country to help with a big puzzle.

What Are "Tricky Games Online"?

Now, let's talk about what these grown-ups are said to have done. It's called 'romance scams,' but for us, we can think of it as 'tricky games online.' Imagine someone pretends to be your friend or someone who cares about you very much on the internet. They might send nice messages and act like they want to be close. But then, after a while, they start asking for money or gifts. They might say they are in big trouble, or they need help, or they are very sick. But it's not true! They just want to get money from kind people by pretending. This is a very sad thing to do because it breaks people's trust. It's like playing a trick on someone's heart and their wallet.

Did you know? It's super important to always talk to a trusted grown-up, like your mom, dad, or a teacher, if someone you don't know asks you for money or gifts online. Grown-ups can help you understand if it's a trick!

What is "Wire Fraud" and "Money-Laundry"?

The police say these six people will talk about two other big words: 'wire fraud' and 'money-laundry.' Let's make them simple! 'Wire fraud' is when someone uses a computer, a phone, or the internet to trick people and get their money. It's like sending a message or making a call that isn't true, all to take someone's hard-earned savings. Imagine someone sends an email saying you won a million toys, but first, you have to send them your pocket money. That's a trick! They use 'wires' like internet cables to send these tricky messages. 'Money-laundry' is a funny name for something not funny at all. Imagine you have some very dirty clothes, and you wash them to make them look clean. 'Money-laundry' is when people get money by doing something bad, like the tricky games online. Then, they try to hide where the money came from. They might buy lots of new things or put it in different bank accounts so it looks like they got the money fairly. But it's still 'dirty' money because it came from a trick!

Did you know? Police officers and special helpers called detectives work very hard to solve these money puzzles. They follow clues to find out who is doing the tricky things and where the 'dirty' money went.

Why Do People Go to Another Country?

So, why are these six grown-ups going all the way to the United States? It's because the people who were tricked live there. And the rules about the internet and money are very important in every country. When someone does something wrong in one country, but the people they hurt are in another country, the two countries can work together. It's like if you borrow a toy from a friend in another town, and you accidentally break it. You would go to their town to say sorry and help fix it, right? Countries do something similar to make sure justice is fair for everyone, no matter where they live. So, South Africa and the United States are working like good friends to solve this big problem.

Did you know? Africa is a very big continent with many, many countries! And countries all over the world often talk to each other and help each other with big problems, just like friends help each other. It's called international cooperation!

What Can We Learn?

This news teaches us a very important lesson: always be careful online! The internet is a wonderful place for learning and playing, but it's also a place where some people might try to play tricks. Remember these golden rules: * **Never share your family's money information or passwords online.** These are like secret keys that only your family should know. * **Always tell a trusted grown-up** if someone you don't know asks for money, gifts, or private information online. * **Be careful about new friends online.** It's hard to know if someone is really who they say they are. * **If something feels wrong, it probably is.** Listen to your gut feeling!

Stay Safe and Smart!

Being smart online means being safe. We want everyone to have fun and learn on the internet, but always with a grown-up nearby to help. The police and judges work hard to make sure our world is safe from tricky games. Let's all do our part by being smart online reporters ourselves! Thank you for listening, and stay curious, kind, and safe!
summary: Six grown-ups from Nigeria, accused of tricking people online to get money, will go from South Africa to the United States to talk to a judge about 'wire fraud' and 'money-laundry.'
whyMatters: This news is important because it teaches us to be very careful and smart when we are online, making sure we don't get tricked by people asking for money or gifts, and to always tell a trusted grown-up if something feels wrong.

originalTitle: More than 20 children killed in DR Congo school fire
title: A Sad Story and Brave Hearts: A School Fire in DR Congo
content:
Hello, Super Friends!

Hello, my wonderful friends all across Africa! I'm your kid-friendly news reporter, and today I have some news that makes our hearts feel a little bit heavy. It's about a sad event that happened in a country called the Democratic Republic of Congo, or DR Congo for short. But even in sad times, we can also find stories of bravery and learning how to keep everyone safe.

What Happened in Bukavu?

Imagine your school, a place where you learn new things, play with your friends, and make amazing drawings. In a city called Bukavu, in DR Congo, there were two schools very close together. One day, something very scary happened: a fire started. Fires are very dangerous and can spread quickly, especially if there are lots of things that can burn, like wooden furniture or paper. When the fire started, everyone wanted to get out of the school very, very fast to be safe. Just like you would in a fire drill!

Learning About a 'Stampede'

Sometimes, when many, many people try to go through a door or a narrow space all at the same time because they are scared and want to be safe quickly, it can be tricky. This is called a 'stampede.' It means lots of people moving quickly together, and sometimes it can cause people to bump into each other or fall down. Sadly, because everyone was trying to leave the burning schools so quickly in Bukavu, some children got hurt. We are very, very sad to say that some children lost their lives in this sad event.

Did you know?

Did you know? Africa is a huge continent, and the Democratic Republic of Congo is one of its very big countries! It's in the middle of Africa, like the heart of our continent, filled with beautiful rivers, forests, and amazing animals!

Who Were the Helpers?

When bad things happen, amazing people always come to help! In Bukavu, when the fire started, grown-ups, teachers, and neighbours rushed to help the children. Firefighters, who are like real-life superheroes, came with their big trucks and hoses to put out the fire. They work very hard to keep us safe from fires. Teachers are always super brave, and they helped guide the children to safety. Even other grown-ups in the community helped to look after the children who made it out, giving them comfort and care.

Learning From Sad Times: Fire Safety

This sad event reminds us why it's so, so important to learn about fire safety. Does your school have fire drills? A fire drill is like a practice run, so everyone knows exactly what to do if there's a fire. You learn where the safe exits are and how to walk calmly outside to a special meeting spot. Always listen carefully to your teachers during a fire drill. They are teaching you how to be safe and smart!

Did you know?

Did you know? A fire alarm makes a very loud noise to tell everyone that there might be a fire! If you hear a fire alarm, it means it's time to follow your teacher's instructions carefully and calmly leave the building.

Helping Hands and Kind Hearts

Even though this happened far away from some of you, we can send our love and kind thoughts to the children and families in Bukavu. When one part of our big African family is sad, we all feel it. It's important to remember that people care and will help each other. Grown-ups, leaders, and helpful organisations will work very hard to help the community heal. They will also think about how to make sure all schools are even safer in the future. Safety is super important, especially in places where children learn and play.

Building Back Stronger

The people in Bukavu are strong and brave. They will help each other. Schools are so important because they are where children learn to read, write, count, and dream big, big dreams for their future. Building new, safer schools will be a very important job, so children can go back to learning and playing in a safe place.

Did you know?

Did you know? Always remember to stop, drop, and roll if your clothes ever catch fire! This helps to put out the flames quickly and keep you safe.

A Message of Hope and Safety

So, my dear friends, while this news is sad, it also reminds us that we must always be careful and learn about safety. Listen to your teachers and grown-ups when they teach you about fire drills and safety rules. Remember to look out for your friends and always be kind. We send all our love and strength to the children, families, and brave helpers in Bukavu, DR Congo. We hope that with kindness and hard work, their schools will be safe and happy places again soon. Keep learning, keep playing, and keep staying safe!
summary: In the city of Bukavu in DR Congo, a sad school fire occurred, and while people tried to escape, some children were hurt; brave helpers rushed to put out the fire and keep everyone safe.
whyMatters: This is important because it reminds us why fire safety, like fire drills at school, is very important to keep all children safe, and it shows us how people help each other when sad things happen.

originalTitle: Royal family rift after popular TV news presenter chosen to succeed Ugandan king
title: A Royal Puzzle: Who Will Be The Next King in Tooro?
content:
Hello, my little friends across Africa! It's your friendly news reporter, Pendo, here! I have a very important story for you today from a wonderful place called Uganda. Imagine a big, beautiful land with green trees and happy people. This land has a special leader called a King. A king helps take care of his people and his land. This special land is called a kingdom.

A Royal Family Puzzle

In Uganda, there is a special kingdom called Tooro. For a very long time, Tooro has had kings. These kings are like very important dads or granddads for the whole kingdom! They help make sure everyone is safe and happy. Kings often have big responsibilities, like making sure there are good schools and roads, and listening to the people's needs. *Did you know?* Uganda is a beautiful country in East Africa! It is famous for its amazing wildlife, like elephants and giraffes, and its friendly people.

When a King Goes Away

Once upon a time, there was a good King in Tooro. Let's call him King David. He was much loved by his people. He worked hard to help everyone in his kingdom. He made sure people had what they needed and that peace stayed in the land. He was a very wise leader. But then, one day, King David passed away. This means he went to be with the stars in the sky. It was a very sad time for everyone in the kingdom. People cried and missed their good king. When a king passes away, someone new needs to become the king. This new king is called the "heir." *Simple Explanation:* An "heir" is like the next person in line. If you have a toy and you say, "When I'm big, my little sister will get this toy," then your sister is the heir to your toy! It means they are chosen to take over after someone else.

Who Will Be The Next King?

Now, here is where our puzzle begins! Everyone in Tooro Kingdom started to wonder: "Who will be our next King? Who will lead us now?" Some people in the kingdom thought of someone new. This person was a very popular TV news presenter. You know, like the friendly people you see on TV telling you the news every day! He was very well-known because he was on television a lot. Many people liked him because he spoke nicely and was famous. They thought, "Maybe he could be our new King because he is popular and smart!"

The Family's Secret Paper

But wait! King David had a family. They were very sad that he was gone, of course. But they had a secret, a very important one. They said King David left a very special paper. This paper is called a "will." *Simple Explanation:* A "will" is like a special letter from someone who has passed away. In this letter, they tell everyone what they want to happen after they are gone. Like who gets their things, or who should take care of important jobs, or who should become the next king. It's their last wish, written down for everyone to see. In King David's will, he wrote down something very important for the kingdom. He said that his own young son should become the next King! Yes, his very own child! This little boy was still quite young, maybe even a child himself.

Two Sides of the Story

So now, we have a big question! Some people think the popular TV presenter should be king because he is well-known and liked. Other people, especially King David's family, say his young son should be king because King David wrote it clearly in his will. This is a very big disagreement! This is what we call a "royal family rift." A "rift" is a big disagreement or a crack between people. Like when two friends can't agree on which game to play, and they feel a bit apart. Here, it's a disagreement among the royal family members and among the people of the kingdom. The family feels very strongly about the will. They believe it's very important to listen to what King David wanted. They want his wishes to be respected. They want his son to follow in his footsteps and become the next leader of Tooro Kingdom.

Why Is It Important?

You might be thinking, "Why is this such a big deal, Pendo? Why can't they just pick someone?" Well, it's a very big deal for a kingdom and its people! Having a king is important for many reasons. A king helps bring everyone together. He helps keep old traditions and stories alive. He is a symbol of the kingdom's history, going back many years, and also a symbol of its future. People look to their king for guidance and unity. If there is disagreement about who should be king, it can make people in the kingdom feel confused or sad. Everyone wants to know who their leader will be. They want peace and clear rules so that life in the kingdom can continue smoothly and happily. *Did you know?* Some kings and queens around the world wear beautiful crowns and special clothes for important ceremonies! These are not just pretty items; they are symbols of their power, their family, and the long traditions of their kingdom.

What Happens Next?

Now, special elders and wise people in the kingdom will have to talk. These elders are very respected because they know a lot about the kingdom's history and rules. They will look at King David's will very, very carefully. They will listen to what the family says, and they will also listen to what the people want and feel. They need to make a fair decision. A decision that follows the old and wise rules and traditions of the Tooro Kingdom. A decision that will bring peace and happiness to everyone. It's a very big job for them to make sure the right person becomes king.

The Young King To Be

Imagine being a little boy, and one day, you might become a king! It's a huge job. You would need to learn so much about leading people, about history, and about making good choices. You would need to be brave, kind, and fair to everyone. If the young son becomes king, he would have many helpers. His family would guide him. Wise elders would teach him everything he needs to know. He would learn how to be a great leader for his people, just like his father, King David. It's a journey of learning and growing. *Did you know?* The real King of Tooro Kingdom today, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, became king when he was only 3 years old! He is one of the youngest kings in the world! Isn't that amazing? He has learned so much since then and is now a grown-up king, caring for his kingdom.

A Lesson in Fairness

This story from Uganda teaches us a lot about fairness and following rules. Even in a big, important kingdom, rules are very important. And family wishes, like those written in a will, are also very, very important. It shows us that everyone wants what is best for their community. Everyone hopes that the people of Tooro Kingdom will find a happy solution. They hope that the new king will be chosen in a way that makes everyone feel good and united. That way, the kingdom can continue to thrive and be a happy place. So, my friends, that's our big news story today! We will keep watching to see who becomes the next King of Tooro Kingdom. Will it be the popular TV presenter, or King David's young son, as written in the special will? It's a royal puzzle indeed! Stay safe and happy, and keep learning new things every day! This is Pendo, your kid-friendly news reporter, signing off from Africa!
summary: A big puzzle is happening in Uganda's Tooro Kingdom: after their old king passed away, some people want a famous TV presenter to be the new king, but the royal family says the king's special paper (his will) says his young son should take over.
whyMatters: This is important because kingdoms need a clear leader to help everyone stay united and follow old traditions, and disagreements about who that leader should be can make people confused or sad.

originalTitle: Houthis take control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, key shipping route
title: Boats, Coasts, and Important Ocean Roads!
content:
Hello, My Wonderful Friends Across Africa!

Hello, hello, my super friends! It’s your friendly news buddy here, ready to share some important news from our big, beautiful continent and beyond. Today, we're going to learn about a place not too far from some parts of Africa, a country called Yemen, and a special part of the ocean. Imagine you have a favorite toy that comes from far away. How does it get to you? Most times, it travels on a very big boat across the ocean! These boats carry everything from yummy snacks to cool new clothes and even your school books. So, paths on the water are super, super important!

Where is Yemen?

Let's start with a little adventure on our imaginary map! Yemen is a country that is like a neighbor to some parts of Africa, just across a big stretch of water. It sits on a special ocean called the Red Sea. If you look at a map, you'll see a big blue space, and Yemen is right there, touching the water. Did you know? The Red Sea is called that because sometimes, tiny little plants in the water can make it look a bit reddish! It's a very pretty and important ocean. Africa also has many amazing coasts, like the sunny beaches in South Africa or the busy ports in Egypt. Just like our coasts, Yemen's coast is a very special place.

Meet the "Houthis"

Now, let's talk about a group of people in Yemen. They are called the "Houthis." Imagine if in your town, a group of friends wanted to be in charge of making decisions for everyone. That’s a bit like the Houthis. They are a group of people who want to lead their land and make rules. Recently, these Houthis moved very quickly, like a fast little ant looking for a new home. They went to a part of Yemen that is right next to the Red Sea. This part is called the "Red Sea coast." They have now taken charge of this area. When we say "taken charge," it means they are now the main people making decisions and looking after things in that part of the country.

The Red Sea Coast: A Special Place for Boats

Why is this Red Sea coast so special? Well, imagine a super busy highway, but for boats! The Red Sea is like that. Many, many boats travel through it every single day. They are carrying all those treasures we talked about – your toys, your food, your clothes, and so much more. This stretch of land, the coast, is where these boats often stop or pass by. It's like a gas station or a rest stop along the highway for cars, but for big ocean ships! So, if someone is in charge of this coast, they can have a say in how boats use that part of the ocean. Did you know? Africa has the longest coastline of any continent! This means we have lots and lots of places where boats can come and go, bringing us goodies and taking our own amazing products to other parts of the world.

Boats and Treasures: Why Roads on Water are Important

We call these paths on the water "shipping routes." Think of them like invisible roads across the ocean. These shipping routes are like the lifelines of the world! Without them, it would be very hard for countries to share things and help each other. When boats travel through a "key shipping route," it means it's a very, very important path. It's like the main road everyone uses because it's the quickest or easiest way. Did you know? Some of the biggest boats in the world are called container ships, and they can carry thousands of big metal boxes filled with goods! It's like a giant floating puzzle of treasures.

Taking Charge: What "Control" Means

So, when the Houthis "take control" of this Red Sea coast, it means they are now in charge of that piece of land. They can decide who comes and goes, and how things work there. For the big boats that sail past, this means the Houthis will be the ones making rules about passage or stops in that area. It's a bit like when you play a game and someone becomes the team leader for a specific area of the game. They get to decide what happens there. This can make things a little bit tricky for the big boats and for all the countries that use this important path.

Another Path for Boats

Sometimes, there's a main road that everyone uses, but then there's also a smaller, less busy road that you can use if the main one gets too crowded or if there's a problem. This is called an "alternative shipping route." The Red Sea path is like one of these very important alternative roads for boats. It's a way for boats to go if another very, very busy path, far away, is difficult to use. It's like having a backup plan, which is always smart! Did you know? Boats have been sailing across oceans for thousands of years! People used to use sails powered by wind, but now many boats have giant engines.

Far Away, Another Busy Road: The Strait of Hormuz

There's another very important, but faraway, busy path for boats called the "Strait of Hormuz." It’s like another super highway for boats, but in a different part of the world. Because it's so busy, and sometimes things can be a bit tricky there, having the Red Sea path open and safe is extra important for boats to have options. This means that the Red Sea route is like a very good friend who helps out when things get a bit tough somewhere else. It helps make sure that all our important things can still travel safely and reach us.

Why This Matters to You and Me

When a very important path for boats has changes, it can sometimes mean that things like your new shoes or your favorite fruit from another country might take a little longer to arrive. It might also mean that the people who send these things have to work a bit harder to find the safest and fastest way. But don't worry! Many smart and kind people around the world work very hard to make sure that these boat paths stay open and safe for everyone. They want to make sure that countries can keep sharing things and helping each other. This news reminds us how connected our world is. What happens in one place, even far away in Yemen, can affect how things move around the globe. It also reminds us that working together and being kind helps everyone. Peace and sharing are always the best ways for countries to get along. Did you know? Some boats carry special goods like oil, which helps power cars and trucks! So, these shipping routes are important for many different types of energy too.

Let's Keep Learning!

Thank you for listening, my wonderful friends! It's super important to learn about the world around us. Remember, even though news can sometimes sound a bit serious, it's all part of understanding how our big, beautiful world works. Let's always hope for peace and kindness everywhere, so all our boats, and all our treasures, can travel safely to their homes. See you next time, and keep smiling!

originalTitle: Japan, India, Ukraine: Why some countries are uneasy about new UN map
title: Map Colors Make Countries Scratch Their Heads!
content:
Hello, hello, my super little explorers from Africa! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, ready to tell you an interesting story from around the world. Today, we're going to talk about something super cool: maps! And guess what? Sometimes, even the colors on a map can make big countries think very, very hard.

What is a Map?

Imagine you have a giant toy car, and you want to draw a picture of it from high up in the sky. That's a bit like what a map is! A map is a special kind of drawing or picture of our Earth, or a part of it. It shows us where countries are, where big oceans stretch wide, where mountains stand tall, and where rivers flow. Maps help us find our way and learn about different places far, far away. Did you know? The very first maps were not on paper! Some were drawn on clay tablets, and some brave sailors even used animal skins to draw their routes across the sea!

The United Nations: A Big Club for Countries

Now, let's talk about a very important group called the United Nations. You can call it the UN for short. Imagine a super-duper big club, but instead of kids, all the countries in the world are members! The UN helps countries be friends, talk to each other, and solve problems together so everyone can live in peace. They also help to make maps to show the world clearly for everyone.

A New Map and Some Colorful Worries

So, the United Nations made a brand new map of the world. It’s a very detailed map! But when some countries looked at it, they got a little bit – let's say – "hmm" about one tiny, tiny thing: the colors that were used for some parts of the land. They are not saying the whole map is bad; they just have questions about certain colors in certain places.

Why Do Colors Matter on a Map?

You might be thinking, "Colors? What's the big deal?" Well, on a map, colors are like secret codes! They are not just for looking pretty. Colors can tell us a lot of things. For example, blue usually means water, green might mean forests, and yellow could mean a desert. But colors can also show which country a certain piece of land belongs to. Imagine you are drawing your favorite animal, and you use one color for its body and another color for its tail. The colors help you see different parts. On a map, if a specific piece of land is colored in a way that usually means it belongs to one country, it can make others wonder why. Did you know? Some maps use very bright colors to show how high mountains are or how deep the oceans are!

Who is "Hmm" and Why?

Countries like Japan, India, and Ukraine are among those who looked at this new UN map and had some questions about the colors. They are not angry, but they are a little "uneasy." This means they are not completely happy with how certain parts of the land are colored on the map. It's a bit like when you and your friend are drawing together, and you both want to use the same special glitter pen for one part of the drawing – you need to talk about it! Sometimes, there are very small pieces of land that two different countries both feel belong to them. It's like two friends both loving the same teddy bear and wanting to keep it. The UN map tries to show everything fairly. But if the map uses a certain color for that "tricky" part of land, it might look like it clearly belongs to only one country. This can make the other country feel a bit sad or worried, because they also believe that land is theirs. Did you know? Japan is an island country, India is a very big country with lots of different languages, and Ukraine is a country in Europe!

What Happens Next?

When countries have these kinds of worries, they don't fight. Oh no! That's what the UN club is for. Instead, they talk! They send messages to each other, and they have meetings. They try to find a color or a way to show the land on the map that everyone agrees on. It's all about being friendly and finding solutions together, just like you would with your friends when you need to share a toy or choose a game. This shows us that even small things, like the color on a map, can be very important to countries. It helps them make sure everyone understands who is who and where is where, so we can all live in a clear and peaceful world.

Why Is This Important for Us in Africa?

Even though Japan, India, and Ukraine are far, far away from our beautiful continent, this story reminds us how important maps are for everyone! In Africa, we have many wonderful countries that work together, too. Understanding how maps work and how countries talk to each other about little things like colors helps us all be good neighbors and friends, not just across Africa, but across our entire big, amazing planet! Did you know? Africa is the second-largest continent in the whole world! It has 54 different countries, each with its own special cultures and stories!
summary: Some countries like Japan, India, and Ukraine are a little worried about the colors used on a new map made by the United Nations, because the colors might make some land look like it belongs to a country they don't agree with, even though they like the rest of the map.
whyMatters: This matters because maps help all countries know where they are and who their neighbors are. If the colors on a map make it look like a piece of land belongs to one country when another country also thinks it's theirs, it can make them uneasy. Talking about it helps countries stay friends and understand each other better, which is good for everyone in the world.

originalTitle: World Athletics Ultimate Championship opens with record $10m prize pot
title: Our African Stars Shine Bright! A Super Sports Party is Here!
content:
Hello, Little Champions!

Hello, amazing little champions! Your kid-friendly news reporter from Africa is here! I have some super exciting news for you today. Get ready to cheer, because a HUGE sports party is about to begin! It's called the "Ultimate Championship." It's like the biggest sports festival you can imagine, just for running, jumping, and throwing! And guess what? It's the very first time this special party is happening! "Inaugural" means it's happening for the first time ever. Isn't that cool? This big event brings together the very best athletes from all over the world to show their amazing skills.

Who Are the Superstars?

At this amazing party, you will see the best athletes in the world! These are men and women who run super fast, jump incredibly high, and throw really far. They are called "Olympic Games champions." This means they have already won big gold medals at other very important races called the Olympic Games. Imagine being the fastest person in the whole world! That's what an Olympic champion is like. They train very, very hard every single day. They wake up early, they eat healthy food, and they practice their running or jumping or throwing. They work so hard to be the best they can be! Did you know? Athletes train for many years to become champions! They are very dedicated and disciplined. They practice in sunshine and sometimes even in the rain! They want to be the best they can be, and they never give up. These superstars inspire us all to try our hardest in everything we do.

A HUGE Prize! What is $10 Million?

Now, here's another exciting part about this big championship. The athletes are not just competing for medals and glory. They are also competing for a "prize pot" of $10 million! Wow! That is a super, super lot of money! It's like having ten million one-dollar notes all stacked up! Can you imagine that many? Did you know? $10 million is enough money to buy many, many footballs or build many new schools! It's a truly enormous amount. This money is given to the champions who run the fastest, jump the highest, or throw the furthest. It's the biggest prize money ever given for this kind of event. That's what "record prize pot" means – more money than ever before! This money helps the athletes a lot. They can use it to buy better training gear, special healthy food, or help their families. Some athletes even use it to build sports centers in their home countries, so more children can play and learn sports! It helps them continue their amazing journey.
